cells.value: Don't put a key in a chat, a file or a log, and never let a script print one. Redaction (hiding part of a value) is done in Python, never with sed.

On 2026-10-01 a sed redaction step printed an old Foreplay key into a session log, because the Mac's sed (BSD sed) has no \s. The key had to be rotated, and the project's pre-approved sed command was removed. A key sweep also found 6 keys in shell history and .env files in 3 project folders, still to move.

Move a new key one way only: Alex copies it, the agent saves it to the 1Password Connectors vault, and the key mover script pushes it to Composio (the hub that holds Alex's app logins). Then prove one call works.

A key pasted into a chat passes through the model, and ChatGPT's sign-in protection doesn't cover secrets pasted in chat. The Claude app and ChatGPT have no 1Password route, so their keys arrive only through Composio. On 2026-10-01 the Foreplay key went this way: read from the clipboard by length only, saved to 1Password, pushed to Composio, and one usage call passed.

Keep every secret an AI or script needs in the Connectors vault, which the connectors-sync robots read. Nothing an AI needs goes in Employee or Private, the default Shared vault, 'Local Vault (operator secrets)' or a 1Password Environment. Agents read 1Password only through the Keychain robot; making robots, Connect servers or vault grants is Alex's (a security setting).

A secret the robots can't reach can only be read as Alex through the 1Password app, with a Touch ID prompt each time. On 2026-10-01 a sweep found 3 client tracking items in 'Local Vault (operator secrets)', 1 dashboard item in Employee, and the Apify and PageSpeed keys and 36 GHL location keys only in Environments, none of which a robot can read. The same day a Cursor chat ran plain op as Alex and saw all 28 vaults.
Don't leave a key in a plain file anywhere on the Mac, ~/Backups included. 1Password holds the only copy; delete a file copy once the 1Password item is proven identical.

The 2026-10-01 parity check found keys in plain files: the Google robot's key (a service account, meaning a robot login, that acts as any of the 16 Workspace users) in 4 files, a second admin-delegated Google key, the GHL gateway key (all 303 sub-accounts) in 2 files, a never-expiring Meta token that can spend, and Orgo keys. The robot copies and ~/.orgo/mcp.env were removed that day; the Meta token file followed on 2026-10-01 after a hash match, with the retired meta CLI (K04); a names-only check at 18:57Z found the GHL gateway key files (K03) and the admin-delegated Google key (K02) still in ~/.cursor/mcp-servers, and ~/.orgo/credentials.json waits on a decision. Since then: K02 done 2026-10-01, K03 done 2026-10-03, and ~/.orgo/credentials.json is gone (names-only check 2026-10-03). Still open: plain-text key copies inside ~/Backups (claims audit 2026-10-03, verify-workbook-other.md §4): 57 key-shaped values, none of them in any 1Password vault (spp-p55a, 2026-10-03); Alex decides per folder (To do R71).

Keep keys in memory only: a wrapper reads the key from 1Password at each run (gcloud_robot.py for Google Cloud, orgo_op.py for Orgo), and checks print only True/False or a fingerprint. Pass keys through stdin, never as command arguments or temp files.

A key file left on disk for a tool is a copy that can leak. On 2026-10-01 the robot wrapper replaced the local gcloud key: the key reaches openssl through a pipe, gcloud gets a 1-hour token, and nothing touches disk. op (1Password's command-line tool) fails inside the Claude Code sandbox (the safety box Claude's commands run in), so these runs happen outside it.

Don't connect any route that lets a chat read a vault item, such as Composio's _1password toolkit or a community 1Password MCP server (a plug-in that gives an AI tools). The official 1Password plugin in ChatGPT only managed Environments, a separate developer feature, and never returned a secret; it was removed on 2026-10-01.

Those routes put the raw key into the chat, which breaks the keys-never-in-chat rule. Composio's _1password toolkit can also create, update and permanently delete vault items. Removed 2026-10-01 on Alex's decision: login ca_PSjKn84-Yd_T paused (INACTIVE) and auth config ac_FFWFZ84tq6l7 disabled at 22:13Z, so a 1Password call through Composio failed with 'No active connection'. Both logins were deleted 2026-10-02 23:04:44Z after Alex's yes naming CG-SZRA (HTTP 200, readback 404), and the disabled auth config on 2026-10-03 11:53Z (readback 404); the robot's token was already dead (2026-10-01 22:40:34Z, 403 Service Account Deleted; To do R59). Composio's login ran as the 1Password robot 'composio' with read and write on 26 vaults, Javar's and every agent vault included, and the toolkit can get, create, update and delete items, so one prompt-injected chat could read or wipe any of them. Prompt injection is measured, not theoretical: in 160 tests across 8 models, agents leaked data in up to 40% of authorized-looking requests and exfiltrated sensitive files in up to 90% (SBSeg 2026); a poisoned public GitHub issue made Claude 4 Opus copy private-repo data into a public pull request through the official GitHub MCP server (Invariant Labs, 2025-05-26).

Don't let a skill's setup steps save a key to a file. The skill calls the app through Composio, or a script reads the key with op at run time.

On 2026-10-01 the ad-recreator skill, which Codex can load, told the AI to save the Atlas Cloud key in a plain file. The file didn't exist yet, so rewording the setup stops the leak before anyone runs it.
Rotate any key that was ever printed or left in a plain file: save the new key through the normal flow, prove a call, then confirm the old key is refused.

A leaked key keeps working until it is rotated. The Foreplay key printed on 2026-10-01 was rotated the same day, and the old key now returns 401 (refused). The Google robot key sat in plain files in 4 places; rotating it is still Alex's call.

Don't use 1Password Environments' local .env destinations, and never open, read, grep, copy or hash a .env file or named pipe. To stop the pop-ups, turn the destination's Enabled toggle off in the 1Password app; no CLI or MCP tool can.

Each destination is a named pipe that pops 1Password's authorization dialog on Alex's screen whenever anything opens it, and 1Password remounts it at every start. On 2026-10-01 a worker opened two of the four dead ones and popped dialogs, so the Director banned opening them; a script that reads one after its mount is off would hang. Opening a pipe for reading also waits until 1Password answers (POSIX open()), so the command stalls until someone approves or denies.

Name the login on every Composio call (--account, or account / user); the app's card names the default. Never run a Composio search result's sample call as is: rebuild it from the schema, because samples can send or spend.

With no login named, Composio uses the most recently changed one, which can be an agent's: unqualified Gmail calls ran as jay@ on 2026-10-01 (Codex guard Run H). gmail_send's sample sets draft_only:false, so a copied call sends the email. In the blind split test (2026-10-01) the 3-bullet App rules block that carries these rules scored 39/40, against 35/40 for the old per-app index.

Models rarely fix their own mistakes and kept their own wrong answer 86% of the time. On 2026-09-30 an independent audit of the rebuilt connectors workbook found 61 issues.

Use one agent for step-by-step work and parallel helpers only for independent parts. Two agents never write the same file: announce a file lock in the consolidation chat and re-read each file fresh before writing.
